findings: WASTED-TURN TAXONOMY on the certified field floor (424 acting turns / 449 analyzer invocations / 1181 LLM generations / 1639 actions): 54.0% of acting turns sit on a level never cleared; 62.1% of generations execute no environment action and carry 49.7% of all generated characters; 53.5% of turns fire exactly one action while 12.2% fire >=8 and carry 46.9% of all actions; 3.8% of generations raise a Python traceback; 7.3% of turns are lost to a client-side Read-timeout. Tool-call FORMAT failures and finish_reason=length are BOTH 0.0% -- those two hypotheses are dead.

PER-TURN ARITHMETIC VERDICT: 195 productive turns -> 28 levels = 6.96 turns/level; the marginal turn (from T1->T3) is worth 0.0141 lc vs the average 0.0660 = 21%. Recovering ALL waste (zero inspection + zero tracebacks + zero timeouts, a physically impossible bound) is a x2.16 budget multiplier, which at the measured epsilon 0.17 is +4.0 lc => lc 32, LB ~1.78. RECOVERING WASTED TURNS CANNOT REACH 2.5. LB 2.50 (lc 45) needs x1.60 value per turn at constant 17 turns/game = converting 52% of the 229 dead turns.

RESOURCE INVERSION: because epsilon=0.17 above our operating point, extra actions are nearly worthless AND therefore nearly free (T3 spent 2184 extra actions for +0.04 mean_score). Score arithmetic bounds a retry policy: going k->k+1 at uniform action ratio r beats staying at k iff r < sqrt((k+2)/k) -- unbounded at k=0, 1.73 at k=1, 1.41 at k=2. 20 of 25 games sit at k<=1, so the retry allowance exists exactly where the levels are.
